findings.claim: classify_credit_score(score: int) has no type check. Its first statement is the range check `if not (300 <= score <= 850): raise ValidationError("credit score must be between 300 and 850")`, followed by the thresholds < 580 POOR, < 670 FAIR, < 740 GOOD, else EXCELLENT. So a float such as 700.5 (or 700.0) passes the range check and returns CreditBucket.GOOD, and True/False (int subclass values 1/0) reach the range check and raise only the out-of-range ValidationError. This file has not yet been changed for this task.
ValidationError is already imported in risk_bands.py from loanflow.errors, and it is defined in loanflow/errors.py as a subclass of LoanflowError.

Money.__post_init__ checks integers with `if isinstance(self.cents, bool) or not isinstance(self.cents, int): raise ValidationError("Money.cents must be an integer number of cents")`. This check is the first statement in __post_init__.

Percentage.__post_init__ uses the same convention: `if isinstance(self.basis_points, bool) or not isinstance(self.basis_points, int): raise ValidationError(...)`. This type check runs before its separate range (negative) check. That is the type-before-range ordering the scope requires.

test_risk_bands.py imports pytest, ValidationError and classify_credit_score. It has test_credit_bucket_boundaries, which uses a dict of 579/580/669/670/739/740 mapped to the expected CreditBucket and asserted with `is`. It also has test_credit_score_out_of_range_is_rejected, which uses separate `with pytest.raises(ValidationError):` blocks for 299 and 851. There is currently no test for float or bool scores.
The only direct production caller of classify_credit_score is build_risk_profile in risk_profile.py. It passes its credit_score: int parameter straight through.

The CLI converts the payload credit score with int(payload["credit_score"]) before passing it to run_pipeline, so the CLI path always gives classify_credit_score a plain int. pipeline.py declares credit_score: int and forwards it.
No in-repo caller or test passes a non-int (float or bool) credit score into classify_credit_score or the paths that reach it.

search_attempts.result: Every literal credit_score value in tests, fixtures and integration tests is an integer (780, 560, 600, 500). The CLI converts with int(). No float or bool credit score was found.

findings.claim: Adding the bool/int type check before the range check should not break any existing test or caller. The current unit and integration suites should stay green once it is added.
findings.reasoning: Every existing test passes integer scores (F-5). The only production caller forwards an int (F-6), and the CLI converts with int() (F-7). A check that rejects only bool and non-int values cannot change the result for any of these existing integer inputs, and leaving the range check and thresholds as they are keeps the 299/851 and boundary behavior.
